full_judgment:
6. Mr. Mahmudul Islam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner company in writ petition No.1971 of 2002 submits that no doubt there is a presumption of correctness of constitutionality of an enactment passed by the parliament but in an appropriate case if it is found that an act passed by the parliament is in breach of the fundamental right guaranteed by the Constitution to the citizens or is arbitrary per se can be knocked down by this Court. In elaborating his submission Mr. Islam relied on the decision reported in AIR1958(SC) 538 with special reference to the principles of law laid down by the Indian Supreme Court in that case as to when the Supreme Court can interfere with an act passed by the parliament or declare it a nullity. Five principles have been laid down in that decision and he relied particularly on the observation of the Indian Supreme. Court that in order to sustain the presumption of constitutionality the court may take into consideration matters of common knowledge, matters of common report, the history of the times and may assume every state of facts which can be conceived existing at the time of legislation and that while good faith and knowledge of the existing conditions on the part of a legislature are to be presumed, if there is nothing on the face of the law or the surrounding circumstances brought to the notice of the court on which the classification may reasonably be regarded as based, the presumption of constitutionality cannot be carried to the extent of always holding that there must be some undisclosed and unknown reasons for subjecting certain individuals or corporation to hostile or discriminating legislation and therefore he urged upon us that the above principles will have to be constantly borne in mind by the court when it is called upon to adjudge the constitutionality of any particular law attacked as discriminatory and violative of the equal protection of the law. Mr. Islam also candidly submitted that like the presumption of correctness and Constitutionality of the Act if some reason is assigned by the executive for making any decision court will take a lenient and liberal view and will not interfere with it but in a case where it is found that an order is issued without any basis whatsoever, that is, in other words, when the executive action per se appears to be arbitrary, a petitioner can question the order as being discriminatory and violative of Article 27 of the Constitution. The learned Advocate further submits that if the stand taken by the respondent No.3 in the earlier writ petition is accepted then the equality clause will be rendered nugatory inasmuch as any order passed without any rational basis and without any objective standard at all will not be amenable to the jurisdiction of this court under Article 102 of the Constitution and in the instant case admitted position is that the respondent No.3 has miserably failed to show any basis either for exempting other electrical appliances from paying VAT and to retain the same on the product of the petitioner and thus the order is per se arbitrary and discriminatory. The learned Advocate further submits that if the contention of the respondent No.3 is accepted that Government is entitled to grant exemption on its subjective satisfaction then the equality before law, which is guaranteed to the petitioner, becomes, meaningless and the citizens will be at the mercy of the executive fiat. 

 9. Ms. Nahid Mahtab, the learned Assistant Attorney General appearing for the respondent No.3 emphatically submits that the notification in question cannot be termed to be discriminatory in nature inasmuch as the classification has been made on a reasonable basis and the members belonging to the same class has been equally treated. Therefore, the exemption granted in respect of other electrical home appliances cannot be tagged in the same class. The exemption granted in respect of air-conditioner, colour Television cannot be treated to be discriminatory in nature for retaining the supplementary duty on refrigerator, an essential household appliance. The learned Assistant Attorney General further submits relying on the decision reported in 41 DLR (AD) 30 that the courts should not insist on delusive exactness or classification in any given case. Classification is justified if it is not palpably arbitrary. There is always a presumption in favour of the constitutionality of a Statute and the burden is upon him who attacks it to show that there has been a clear transgression of the Constitutional principles and this rule is based on the assumption, judicially recognised and accepted, that the Legislature understands and correctly appreciates the needs of its own people, that its laws are directed to problems made manifest by experience and that its discriminations are based on adequate grounds. Ms. Nahid Mahtab, the learned Assistant Attorney General further submits relying on an observation made by the Indian Supreme Court in the case of Federation of Hotel and Restaurant v. Union of India and others AIR 1990(SC) 1664 the principles of which has been quoted by the Pakistan Supreme Court in the case of M/S. Elahi Cotton Mills and others, appellants, v. Federation of Pakistan and others, respondents, reported in PLD 1997(SC) 582 held courts, while interpreting laws relating to economic activities, view the same with grater latitude then the laws relating to civil rights such as freedom of speech religion etc., keeping in view the complexity of economic problems which do not admit of solution through any doctrine or strict socket formula. She then submits that although Article 27 of the Constitution is not outside the ambit of taxing legislation but in interpreting the revenue law the court will take into consideration several facts in examining the allegation of discrimination and if there is not found any irregularity or infirmity the law will not be discriminatory. The learned Assistant Attorney General then contends that Government has been authorised by section 14(1) of the Act to exempt anybody from payment of VAT and in exercise of that authority the Government in respect of other electrical appliances exempted them from payment of supplementary duty but they have retained supplementary duty on the locally manufactured refrigerator and since the action is within the power of the Government the court cannot go beyond the order to see the reason behind it and by issuing the notification the Government has not acted beyond their jurisdiction inasmuch as delegation is authorized by Article 61(1) of the Constitution read with section 14(1) of the Act. Therefore, the notification has been issued in exercise of the authority vested in the Government and all the manufacturers of refrigerator has been classified in one group while the manufacturers of other electrical appliances have been brought in a different group and the Government is competent to do so. The learned Assistant Attorney General frankly conceded that demands made by the VAT authority pursuant to Annexure 'D' of writ petition No. 1971 of 2002 is illegal and without jurisdiction as it conflicts with the parent law, namely, VAT Act read with third schedule. She then submits that this point was taken in writ petition No. 1971/2002 and was agitated at the time of hearing by Mr. Mahmudul Islam but this point was not taken by the writ petitioner in the earlier writ petition, namely writ petition No. 28 of 2002. The learned Assistant Attorney General further submits that the power conferred upon the Government either under section 14(1) or section 7(1) of the VAT Act is discretionary but it is not absolutely unrestricted and pursuant to that authority the Government must act within the act in a reasonable way and in the instant case Government exercised its discretion in a reasonable way, therefore, by no stretch of imagination the notification can be said to be ultra vires of the Act. 

 Bruen J, in Gulf Colorado Rly. V Ellis, 165 U.S. 150, warned against carrying this presumption too far and observed. 

 "To carry the presumption to the extant of holding that there must be some undisclosed and unknown reason for subjecting certain individual or corporations to hostile and discriminatory legislation is to make the protection clause of 14th Amendment a mere rope of sand." 

 22. Now let us consider the case in the light of the aforesaid principles. It is now well settled that an Act can be valid and a notification issued under the Act may be unconstitutional or ultra vires of the Act. To cut the things short it must be borne in mind that here we are not concerned with the Constitutionality of the Act. The vires of the Act is not disputed. Both the petitioners have challenged the validity of the notification. The principal ground urged in support of the contention as to the invalidity of the notification is founded on Art. 27 of the Constitution. The other ground is that admittedly the VAT was exempted at the import stage but now VAT has been demanded on the sale price of the product which is illegal and without jurisdiction inasmuch as the benefit which was given at the import stage has been taken away by the impugned demands. We have already noticed that electrical appliances like colour Television, Air conditioner etc. has been exempted from payment of VAT whereas it is retained on locally manufactured refrigerators. Classification does not appear to be rational or reasonable. The affluent part of the society has been conferred benefit at the cost of the ordinary common people. No reason has been assigned or could be assigned by the Government for such differential treatment. It is contended by the learned Assistant Attorney General that on subjective satisfaction the Government has done so. We find ourselves in difficulty to argue with her. The decisions on which the learned Assistant Attorney General has relied on, clearly show that in interpreting fiscal law grater latitude has to be given but nevertheless if the same class of property similarly situated is subject to an incidence of taxation which results in inequality amongst holder of the same kind of property it is liable to be struck down on account of infringement of the fundamental right to equality. Here we are confronted with a situation where luxurious electrical appliances including foreign manufactured refrigerator are exempted from supplementary duty whereas for locally manufactured refrigerator the same is retained whereas the product of the petitioners has been discriminated against and that too without considering their case. It appears from the relevant note sheets of the NBR that it was not within the knowledge of the NBR that there are local manufacturer of refrigerator and there is an indication that if it were within their knowledge they would have withdrawn the supplementary duty from the item in question. We also do not find any reasonable basis for segregation of locally manufactured refrigerator from imported refrigerator and other electrical home appliances. We are conscious that the Government is empowered to impose supplementary duty and also can withdraw supplementary duty from any item. But in doing so they must act reasonably and within the ambit of the law. It is apparent that all electrical appliances are exempted from supplementary duty whereas the product of the petitioners has been discriminated against and that too without considering their case. It appears from the relevant note sheets of the NBR that it was not within the knowledge of the NBR that there is local manufacturer of refrigerator and there is an indication that if it were within their knowledge they would have withdrawn the supplementary duty from the item in question. Thus there is no reasonable nexus between the object of the Act and the notification. The notification in question is therefore ultra vires of the Act and must be struck down as the benefit given by the Act is taken away by the notification. It is now well settled that a delegated legislation must be consistent with the parent Act and can not take away the benefit granted by the parent Act. The respondents are demanding supplementary duty and VAT on the full value of the refrigerator assembled by the petitioners pursuant to the impugned S.R.O. The effect of demand is that the exemption granted by the Act itself in respect of the import of refrigerator in CKD condition is to-tally nullified and rendered the exemption granted by the Act meaningless. To this extant the impugned S.R.O.(Annexure B & respectively) is inconsistent with the parent Act and as such the impugned S.R.O. so far as it nullifies the exemption granted by the parent Act from payment of supplementary duty is ultra vires to the parent Act and is therefore void and unenforceable. It further appears that the respondents acted in a discriminatory manner when they have allowed 100% waiver of supplementary duty vide the impugned S.R.O. dated 7.6.01 on the products like Air-Conditioner, colour Television and other electrical appliances including all audio and video equipment’s while retaining full 35% supplementary duty on the production of refrigerator which has become an essential item in one's daily life. It thus appears that arbitrary imposition of 35% supplementary duty and the discriminatory manner of doing it only in case of refrigerator and not in case of all other electrical appliances made in Bangladesh from CKD condition not only offends Art. 27 of the Constitution but also amounts to an unreasonable and unlawful restraint of trade and business and thus is also violative of Art. 40 of the Constitution. In taking the aforesaid view we are not oblivion of the fact that while good faith and knowledge of the existing conditions on the part of the Government are to be presumed. But if there is nothing on the face of the record or the surrounding circumstances brought to the notice of the Court on which the classification is said to be based or the exemption granted, the presumption of Constitutionality of the notification can not be carried to the extent of always holding that there must be some undisclosed and unknown reasons for subjecting certain individuals or corporations to hostile or discriminating treatment. The view taken by us also gets support from the observation of Bruen J. in Gulf Colorado Rly V Elles (165 U.S 150)
